overview.summary: The Patient module is the single public-facing, unauthenticated entry point of the EPTTS mobile app, sitting at the very end of the serialized pharmaceutical supply chain (Manufacturer -> Distributor -> Branch -> Pharmacy -> Patient). It allows any member of the public — with no account, login, or Keycloak SSO — to verify that a dispensed medicine pack is legitimate and to see its supply-chain/authenticity status by scanning its GS1/SGTIN barcode. This is the only role in the app that bypasses authentication entirely, and it exposes by far the smallest surface area (a single tile, one scanner screen) since it is a consumer trust/verification tool rather than an operational supply-chain workflow.
overview.rolesInvolved: Patient / general public — no account, credentials, or Keycloak SSO required. Accessed via the secondary 'Patient' button on the landing screen (as opposed to the primary 'Sign In' button used by all staff roles: Pharmacy, Branch, Distributor, Inspector). There are no sub-roles within Patient; it is a single anonymous, unauthenticated experience.
overview.mainWorkflows:
1) Entry: On the landing screen, tap 'Patient' (secondary button, alongside primary 'Sign In'). This bypasses Keycloak SSO entirely — no credentials are requested.

2) Patient Home: Screen shows header title 'Patient' and subtitle 'Verify your medication', plus a single 'Validate Pack' tile (a clickable parent android.view.View whose child view carries the content-desc 'Validate Pack'; tapping the child propagates the click to the parent) and a 'Back' tile/button to return to the landing screen.

3) Validate Pack flow: Tap 'Validate Pack' -> the Validate Pack Scanner screen opens, showing a page title 'Validate Pack', a Back button (content-desc 'Back', tooltip-text 'Back'), a scan circle (android.view.View, no content-desc — requires coordinate tap or UiAutomator to interact with, since there is no identifiable content-desc), and a label below the circle reading 'Tap to scan GTIN / SGTIN'. The camera preview + scan frame opens when the scan circle is tapped. Point the camera at a GS1/SGTIN barcode on a medicine pack -> the app reads the barcode and displays inline validation results covering pack authenticity and supply-chain status. Tap Back to return to the Patient Home screen; tap Back again to return to the Landing screen.

4) Cannot access: shipments, returns, or EPCIS history — Patient is verification-only and has no visibility into any operational/internal supply-chain screens available to staff roles.
overview.businessRules: Patient access requires no authentication whatsoever and bypasses Keycloak SSO entirely, unlike every staff role (Pharmacy, Branch, Distributor, Inspector) which requires Sign In. The Validate Pack flow is read-only/verification-only — it never creates, modifies, or submits any supply-chain transaction (no EPCIS event is implied to be generated by a Patient scan, unlike Dispense/Receive/Return actions performed by staff). Scanning an unrecognised barcode should display an appropriate error message (exact copy not verified/TBD). No network / server unreachable should show a graceful offline error state (expected behavior, not fully verified). No camera permission: the app should request permission, and if denied, show a fallback message (expected behavior, not fully verified). A manual entry alternative to camera scanning (typing a serial number/SGTIN) is mentioned as a possibility but is explicitly marked conditional ('if supported') — not confirmed to exist in the UI.

keyFields.name: Barcode format
keyFields.values: GS1 / SGTIN (GTIN + Serial Number) DataMatrix/2D barcode on the medicine pack

keyFields.name: Validation result
keyFields.values: Pack authenticity + supply-chain status (inline display, exact fields/labels not itemised in source)

keyFields.name: Entry point
keyFields.values: 'Patient' button on landing screen (secondary to 'Sign In')

overview.openQuestions: The exact content/labels of the 'validation results' screen (what authenticity/status values look like, e.g. whether it mirrors statuses like Dispensed/Active/Recalled) are not itemized in the workflow.md — only described generically as 'validation results (pack authenticity, supply chain status)'. Whether a manual barcode-entry alternative to the camera scanner exists is explicitly conditional/unconfirmed ('if supported'). The exact error message shown for an unrecognised barcode, no-network state, and denied camera permission are all described as expected/edge-case behavior rather than verified observations — precise copy is TBD. Whether a Patient scan generates any backend/EPCIS record is not stated either way.
